result: Trophoblast organoids (TOs) and decidua organoids (DOs) were successfully generated from mid-to-late gestation (26-41 weeks) human placentas. Despite the known decrease in trophoblast stem/progenitor cells after the first trimester, organoids were isolated from all 15 unique placentas, with Ki67-positive proliferative cells identified in full-term chorionic villi.
evaluation: Claims C1-C5 provide converging evidence for successful organoid generation from mid-to-late gestation tissue. The presence of Ki67-positive cells (C4) validates the existence of progenitor cells in full-term tissue, supporting the feasibility of organoid generation (C1, C2). The high proliferative capacity (C5) confirms organoid viability. The citation to prior work (C3) appropriately contextualizes the challenge overcome.

result: TOs and DOs express distinct tissue-specific markers and secrete characteristic factors. TOs express trophoblast markers (SIGLEC6, SDC-1) and secrete hCG, while DOs express decidual markers (MUC5AC) and secrete MUC16. The apical surface of the syncytiotrophoblast in TOs is inward-facing, consistent with first trimester organoids.
evaluation: Claims C6-C12 collectively demonstrate that TOs and DOs recapitulate their tissues of origin through multiple complementary markers. Immunofluorescence (C6-C8), functional secretion assays (C10-C12), and 3D structural analysis (C9) provide robust, multi-modal validation. The consistency with prior first trimester organoid models (C9) strengthens the interpretation.

result: TOs can be differentiated into an EVT-enriched phenotype, with HLA-G positive cells increasing from ~18% to ~96%, accompanied by elevated MMP-2 secretion consistent with EVT characteristics.
evaluation: Claims C13-C14 demonstrate successful EVT differentiation through quantitative immunofluorescence and functional secretion assays. The citation to prior work (C15) validates MMP-2 as an appropriate EVT marker. The dramatic increase in HLA-G positive cells provides strong evidence for differentiation efficiency.

result: TOs and DOs exhibit distinct transcriptional profiles. TOs express placental markers (HSD3B1, XAGE2/3, GATA3, ERVW-1, PSGs, CGA) and placenta-specific microRNAs (C19MC family), while DOs express decidual markers (MUC1, MUC5A/B, SOX17, HOXB8). TOs cluster with first trimester placental tissue and express first trimester-associated factors like KISS1.
evaluation: Claims C16-C26 provide comprehensive transcriptional validation through RNASeq, qPCR, and comparative analyses. The differential expression patterns (C16-C20), tissue-specific microRNA expression (C21-C22), sex-specific gene expression (C23), and clustering with first trimester tissue (C24-C26) collectively demonstrate that organoids recapitulate their tissues of origin. The citations appropriately support prior knowledge claims.

result: TOs and DOs exhibit distinct basal immunological secretomes. TOs secrete only IL-6, IFN-λ2, and three soluble receptors, while DOs release 21 immune factors including CXCL1, CXCL5, and IL-8. This recapitulates secretory phenotypes observed in primary cells and tissue explants.
evaluation: Claims C27-C29 demonstrate differential secretomes through comprehensive Luminex profiling and PCA analysis. The consistency with prior work on primary cells and explants (C30-C31) validates the biological relevance of the organoid models. The stark difference in secretome complexity between TOs and DOs is well-documented.

result: TOs constitutively secrete type III IFN (IFN-λ2) but not type I IFNs or IFN-λ1, recapitulating the unique phenotype of primary human trophoblasts. DOs do not basally secrete IFNs. TO-derived conditioned media induces ISGs and protects non-placental cells from ZIKV infection. EVT-differentiated TOs show reduced IFN-λ2 secretion, suggesting EVTs are not the primary producers.
evaluation: Claims C32-C40 and C70-C73 provide comprehensive evidence for constitutive IFN-λ2 secretion from TOs through Luminex assays (C32-C35), functional reporter assays (C36), and antiviral protection experiments (C37-C38). The comparison to primary cells (C34, C70) and the EVT differentiation experiment (C39-C40) strengthen the interpretation. The citations appropriately contextualize this unique trophoblast feature (C72-C73).

result: TOs and DOs differentially respond to poly I:C treatment. TOs upregulated 448 transcripts including chemokines (CXCL5, CX3CL1, CCL22) and type I IFNs, while DOs upregulated 121 transcripts including CD38 and PLA1A. Only 69 transcripts (mostly ISGs) were shared. Both organoid types induced type III IFNs (IFN-λ1/λ2), which were the top induced factors in DOs.
evaluation: Claims C41-C50 demonstrate organoid-specific responses to TLR3 activation through comprehensive RNASeq and Luminex profiling. The differential transcriptional responses (C42-C46), protein secretion patterns (C47-C50), and limited overlap (C43) are well-documented. The consistency between transcriptional and protein data strengthens the conclusions.

result: DOs are highly permissive to HCMV infection (both AD169r and TB40E strains), while TOs are largely resistant. HCMV-associated factors (RNA4.9, UL63) are significantly lower in TOs. EVT differentiation does not enhance HCMV infection in TOs, suggesting EVTs are not primary targets.
evaluation: Claims C51-C56 demonstrate differential HCMV susceptibility through fluorescence microscopy (C51-C52), RNASeq (C53-C54), and EVT differentiation experiments (C55-C56). The use of two HCMV strains strengthens the conclusions. The inference that EVTs are not primary targets (C56) is appropriately supported by the differentiation experiment (C55).

result: TOs and DOs exhibit distinct transcriptional responses to HCMV infection. TOs differentially expressed 282 (AD169r) or 173 (TB40E) transcripts, while DOs expressed 95 (AD169r) or 117 (TB40E) transcripts. Only 3-4% of transcripts were shared, with only three (CCNA1, OAS2, EPSTI1) induced by both strains in both organoid types. TO-specific transcripts included PRAME family members and TRIM49A/B, while DO-specific transcripts included nitric oxide pathway components (NOS2, DUOX2, DUOXA2) and CXCL10.
evaluation: Claims C57-C62 demonstrate organoid-specific transcriptional responses through comprehensive RNASeq analysis. The minimal overlap (C59-C60) and distinct response signatures (C61-C62) are well-documented. The use of two HCMV strains provides robustness to the findings.

result: TOs and DOs exhibit distinct cytokine responses to HCMV infection. TOs secreted pentraxin-3, IL-8, and IL-11, while DOs secreted proinflammatory cytokines/chemokines (CXCL10, MIP-1α/β, IL-6) and IFN-λ2 but not other IFNs. These responses recapitulate findings from ex vivo tissue explants and isolated trophoblasts.
evaluation: Claims C63-C66 and C75-C76 demonstrate differential cytokine responses through Luminex profiling. The consistency with prior ex vivo studies (C75-C76) validates the biological relevance. The citations appropriately support prior knowledge (C64) and contextualize the findings.

result: Type III IFNs control HCMV infection in DOs but not TOs. Ruxolitinib (JAK inhibitor) treatment significantly increased HCMV replication in DOs but not in TOs, suggesting additional IFN-independent factors restrict HCMV infection in trophoblasts.
evaluation: Claims C67-C68 demonstrate differential IFN dependence through pharmacological inhibition experiments. The inferences about IFN control in DOs (C77) and additional restriction factors in TOs (C78) are appropriately supported by the differential ruxolitinib responses. However, the mechanism of TO resistance remains incompletely defined.

result: Co-culturing TOs and DOs significantly reduces HCMV infection in DOs compared to singly cultured DOs, demonstrating that trophoblast-derived factors (including IFN-λ) protect decidual cells from HCMV infection in a paracrine manner.
evaluation: Claims C69, C80, and C97 demonstrate paracrine protection through a co-culture model. The significant reduction in DO infection when co-cultured with TOs (C69) supports the inference of paracrine protection (C80, C97). However, the specific factors mediating protection beyond IFN-λ are not definitively identified.

result: The manuscript appropriately cites and contextualizes prior work on trophoblast biology, organoid models, HCMV infection, immune responses at the maternal-fetal interface, and limitations of existing models.
evaluation: Claims C3, C15, C22, C26, C30-C31, C54, C64, C70-C74, C79, C81-C92 represent citations to prior work that appropriately contextualize the current study. These citations support background knowledge, validate marker choices, and position the current work within the existing literature. No obvious misattributions or incorrect citations are apparent.

result: The manuscript provides appropriate background on the maternal-fetal interface, its cellular composition, functions, and vulnerability to congenital infections.
evaluation: Claims C93-C104 represent general background knowledge statements that appropriately introduce the biological context. These claims are supported by established scientific knowledge and set up the rationale for the study.
